title: Where to Buy Silver Online Safely

segments.text: MOST SILVER SCAMS FAIL ONE CHECK
segments.narration: Most online silver scams fail one simple check: a working phone and a real address on Google Maps.

Verifying any online silver dealer takes 5 minutes. You need a real street address, a working phone, https on checkout, and reviews spanning multiple years. APMEX, JM Bullion, and SD Bullion pass all four. Most fraudulent listings fail the first two.
segments.explanation: A real street address, working phone, SSL checkout, and multi-year review history covers the main checks

segments.narration: Most dealers add 3 to 4 percent for card payments. That fee buys chargeback rights if the order goes wrong. For your first order with any dealer, pay by card regardless. Once you confirm the dealer ships legitimate silver, switch to check or ACH and keep that 3 to 4 percent as metal.
segments.explanation: Card payments add 3-4% but provide chargeback rights if the order is wrong

segments.narration: Wire transfers offer zero buyer protection. Once the money leaves, it is gone. Fraudulent sellers often demand wire or crypto as the only option. That demand alone is a reason to walk away and find a different dealer.
segments.explanation: Wire transfers offer no buyer protection once sent. Fraudulent sellers often demand wire-only payment

segments.narration: When silver arrives, weigh it immediately. One troy oz is 31.1 grams. If your 1 oz round weighs 28 grams, you received a fake. A digital scale accurate to 0.1 grams costs under $10 and confirms every order in 10 seconds.
segments.explanation: Weigh every delivery. One troy oz equals exactly 31.1 grams. Off-weight means fake

segments.narration: APMEX and JM Bullion compete on fractions of a percent. A listing 10 percent below their prices is not a deal. It is either counterfeit, misrepresented, or a non-delivery setup. Check any unusual price against two established dealers before you buy.
segments.explanation: Silver dealer premiums compete within fractions of a percent. Any listing 5%+ below market signals a problem

segments.narration: Seven red flags cover nearly every silver scam. No physical address. No working phone. Wire or crypto only. No buy-back program. Domain under 2 years old. No SSL on checkout. And reviews that all appeared in the last 30 days. Any single one means find a different dealer.
segments.explanation: Seven warning signs identify nearly all fraudulent online silver sellers before you pay

segments.narration: The Industry Council for Tangible Assets is the USA precious metals trade body. ICTA membership isn't required by law, but most established dealers have it. Verify on their website in under a minute. It signals the dealer operates under professional conduct standards, not just an anonymous storefront.
segments.explanation: ICTA is the USA precious metals trade body. Member dealers operate under professional conduct standards

segments.title: Relative Fraud Risk by Purchase Channel (Lower Is Better)
segments.narration: Established online dealers carry the lowest fraud risk of any purchase channel. Local shops and coin shows are also low. eBay and marketplace listings run medium to high because purity and seller legitimacy are harder to confirm. Anonymous social media listings carry the highest risk of any channel.
